France / CITY EDIT

Ten cities to start with.

Compare the city guide ↗
01 / France

Paris

Paris combines Seine-side landmarks with major art collections and distinctive neighbourhoods.

Explore Paris ↗02 / France

Lyon

Lyon brings together Renaissance streets, silk-working heritage and traditional bouchon restaurants.

Explore Lyon ↗03 / France

Marseille

Marseille centres its Mediterranean maritime identity on a working harbour and hillside neighbourhoods.

Explore Marseille ↗04 / France

Nice

Nice pairs a Mediterranean seafront promenade with the narrow streets and markets of its old town.

Explore Nice ↗05 / France

Bordeaux

Bordeaux combines grand stone architecture along the Garonne with a strong wine culture.

Explore Bordeaux ↗06 / France

Strasbourg

Strasbourg blends Alsatian timber-framed streets, canals and a monumental Gothic cathedral.

Explore Strasbourg ↗07 / France

Toulouse

Toulouse's pink-brick historic centre links grand civic architecture with Romanesque religious heritage.

Explore Toulouse ↗08 / France

Lille

Lille combines Flemish-influenced architecture with lively squares and the brick streets of its old town.

Explore Lille ↗09 / France

Nantes

Nantes turns its Loire-side industrial heritage into a setting for public art and mechanical creatures.

Explore Nantes ↗10 / France

Dijon

Dijon preserves the architectural legacy of Burgundy's dukes in a compact historic centre.

Explore Dijon ↗
